title: Inverse Reinforcement Learning with Switching Rewards and History Dependency for Characterizing Animal Behaviors
page_convention: 1-based PDF pages; printed paper pages unless explicitly stated otherwise
summary: First-emission omission changes an admissible model's likelihood and posterior; minus-gradient update lowers the positive expected log joint. Correct release is counterevidence against empirical-failure claims.
supported_impact: Two Major derivation findings tied directly to core EM inference/learning; historical experiments remain unadjudicated.

problems.title: The forward boundary omits the first action likelihood

original_claim.location: PDFp14 AppendixA2, forward definition, initialization and terminal formulas; jointp13
original_claim.text: alpha_t is the joint through action t, but alpha_1 is set to the initial mode prior alone.

assumptions: Finite three-state, two-action, two-mode model; historyL1; gamma.95; temperature1.
Initial state o certain; mode prior(.5,.5); identity mode kernel permitted by stated assumptions.
Derived optimal soft policies give first action probabilities(.75,.25) and terminal action probability.5.
problems.check: Exact enumeration for ((o,a),(u,a)) yields joint weights3/16,0,0,1/16, likelihood1/4 and terminalposterior(3/4,1/4). Printed alpha1prior gives likelihood1/2 andterminalposterior(1/2,1/2). Independent softBellman residual0 atusedprecision.
problems.result: The printed E-step yields wrong likelihood and posterior inside the model domain.
counterevidence: Correct generative joint includes the factor.
Pinned release alpha0=log(pi0)+log_likes[0] includes it and uses next emissions backward.
The example uses betaT=1, avoiding the ambiguous separate backward boundary.
No historical empirical result is shown wrong.
problems.core_dependency: E-step posterior weights define mode segmentation, reward fitting and mode-transition fitting in mainEqs1–4/AppendixA1.
problems.impact: Major central mathematical inference error; bounded to published specification.

correction.statement: Initialize with p(s1)p(z1)pi_z(a1|s1^L); align backward indices with the joint.
correction.verification: Corrected forward result matches exact enumeration; no full empirical repair.

problems.title: The M-step descends a positive expected log joint

original_claim.location: PDFp12 Algorithm1 and AppendixA1 Eqs5–7; p13argmax
original_claim.text: G is expected log joint to maximize, but update is theta<-theta-eta gradG.

assumptions: Positive step eta and nonzero gradient.
Use exact E-step posteriorq=.75, independent ofP1error.
Initialmodeprior sigmoid(theta) is learned parameter; othercomponents heldfixed forscalarblock.
problems.check: G=.75logsigmoid(theta)+.25log(1-sigmoid(theta)),G'(0)=.25. Printeddescent decreasesG for eta.005,.1,1. Taylor expansion gives -eta||gradG||² forsmallsteps generally.
problems.result: At eta1 Gfallsfrom-.693147 to-.763439; correctedascent reaches-.638439. Small eta.005 also strictlylowersG.
counterevidence: Released transition/emission losses minimize -expectedlogjoint/T; prior uses posteriorcounts.
No loss reduction in actual historical runs is alleged.
problems.core_dependency: Central EM learning update for rewards and hiddenmode dynamics.
problems.impact: Major invalid core learning direction; easy sign repair and valid release do not remove printed derivation error.

correction.statement: Use ascent onG or descent on explicitly defined-G.
correction.verification: Correct direction raisesG at testedsteps; no convergence or empirical performance theorem.

limitations: No trained-model inference, author code execution, raw-data reproduction or historical code-to-result matching.
Animal preprocessing, neural traces, causal biology and complete statistical selection effects not independently verified.
External cited sources and later errata not comprehensively audited; IQ-Learn extension not independently rederived.
Extra OpenReview-only attachments unavailable; serialized datasets/weights not staged.
unresolved_claims: Effect, if any, on reported empirical runs.
Complete historical algorithm version and raw-data/model correspondence.
General convergence and empirical validity of proposed repairs.
repair_verification: Corrected forward boundary matches exact enumeration; ascent increases finite objective. No empirical or global optimization repair claimed.
